sets.title: Set 1: Original Exam Questions
sets.description: The original MCQs from the February 2026 Class Health Care Support Assistant College Final Exam, Cicely McDonnell College of Health Sciences (12 August 2026), Multiple Choice Questions Q28 to Q47. Q1 to Q7 are not included because page 2 of the paper was not available. Q30 is a matching question (Larynx and Nose against their functions), listed as two questions, (a) and (b).

questions.text: A fluid that acts as a shock absorber to protect the brain and the spinal cord is:
questions.explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid (B) is correct because CSF surrounds and cushions the brain and spinal cord in the subarachnoid space, protecting them from impact, and also supplies nutrients and removes waste. Blood (A) and plasma (D) transport substances, and lymphatic fluid (C) is part of the immune and drainage system.

questions.text: An organ that is supplied by olfactory nerve is:
questions.explanation: Nose (C) is correct because the olfactory nerve (cranial nerve I) carries the sense of smell from the nose to the brain. The ear (A) is supplied by the vestibulocochlear nerve, the eye (B) by the optic nerve, and the tongue (D) by the facial and glossopharyngeal nerves for taste.

questions.text: Matching question: Match the body parts in Column A with their function in Column B. Which function belongs to the LARYNX?
questions.explanation: Voice production (B) is correct because the larynx (voice box) contains the vocal cords, which vibrate as air passes through to produce sound. The sense of smell (A) belongs to the nose, and gaseous exchange (C) takes place in the alveoli of the lungs.

questions.text: Matching question: Match the body parts in Column A with their function in Column B. Which function belongs to the NOSE?
questions.explanation: Sense of smell (A) is correct because the olfactory receptors in the upper part of the nasal cavity detect smells and send impulses through the olfactory nerve. The nose also warms, filters and moistens air, but it is not the site of gaseous exchange (C), which occurs in the alveoli. Voice production (B) is the function of the larynx.

questions.text: A part of the brain that controls and coordinates body movement is:
questions.explanation: Cerebellum (A) is correct because it coordinates voluntary movement, balance, posture and muscle tone, making movements smooth. The hypothalamus (B) controls temperature, hunger, thirst and hormones, the medulla oblongata (C) controls heart rate, breathing and blood pressure, and the cerebrum (D) is responsible for thinking, memory and starting voluntary movement.

questions.text: The layer of the skin that has arrector pili muscle is:
questions.explanation: Dermis (C) is correct because the dermis contains hair follicles with the arrector pili muscles (which cause goose bumps), sweat and sebaceous glands, blood vessels and nerve endings. The epidermis (D) is the outer layer without blood vessels, and the subcutaneous layer and hypodermis (A, B) are the same deep layer of fat.

questions.text: The gland responsible for thermoregulation is:
questions.explanation: Sweat glands (B) are correct because they release sweat onto the skin, and when it evaporates it cools the body, helping to control body temperature. Sebaceous glands (A) produce oil (sebum), the adrenal glands (C) produce cortisol and adrenaline, and the parathyroid glands (D) regulate calcium.

questions.text: Sperm cells are produced by the:
questions.explanation: Testes (D) is correct because sperm are made in the seminiferous tubules of the testes. They then mature and are stored in the epididymis (B), travel through the vas deferens (A) and ejaculatory duct (C) and leave through the urethra.

questions.text: What is the function of platelets?
questions.explanation: Stops bleeding (A) is correct because platelets (thrombocytes) stick together at a damaged blood vessel to form a plug and start the clotting process. White blood cells fight infection (B), plasma transports nutrients (C), and red blood cells carry oxygen (D).

questions.text: In the kidneys blood filtration occurs at the:
questions.explanation: Glomerulus (D) is correct because blood is filtered under pressure in the glomerulus, a cluster of capillaries inside Bowman's capsule, forming the filtrate. The proximal tubule (A) reabsorbs most useful substances, the loop of Henle (B) concentrates urine, and the distal tubule (C) fine-tunes salt, water and acid-base balance.

questions.text: The function of thyroid gland is:
questions.explanation: Control metabolism (C) is correct because the thyroid gland secretes thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), which control the body's metabolic rate, growth and energy use. Parathyroid hormone (A) and calcium regulation (B) are functions of the parathyroid glands (the thyroid also makes calcitonin), and sodium regulation (D) is mainly done by aldosterone from the adrenal glands.

questions.text: Mechanical digestion occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Mouth and Stomach (C) is correct because mechanical digestion is the physical breakdown of food: chewing by the teeth in the mouth and churning by the muscular stomach wall. The small intestine also has segmentation movements, but the best pairing among the options is mouth and stomach. The other options pair these with parts of the small intestine (duodenum, ileum), which are mainly sites of chemical digestion and absorption.

questions.text: Self-esteem is defined as:

options.A: An individual subjective evaluation of their own worth or value
options.B: A mental picture of your physical appearance, personality, and characteristics
options.C: The ability to express your needs, thoughts, and feelings clearly and confidently
options.D: The ability to regulate one's own behaviors, thoughts, and emotions in a productive way

questions.explanation: An individual subjective evaluation of their own worth or value (A) is correct because self-esteem is how much a person values and respects themselves. A mental picture of your appearance and personality (B) is self-image. Expressing needs and feelings clearly and confidently (C) is assertiveness, and regulating behaviour, thoughts and emotions (D) is self-regulation.

questions.text: Regarding emotional intelligence, which of the following scenarios best demonstrates effective self-regulation?

options.A: Blaming others for your mistakes to protect your ego
options.B: Ignoring negative feelings completely so they don't bother you
options.C: Expressing every emotion that you feel, the exact moment you feel it
options.D: Taking deep breaths to calm down before responding to an angry email

questions.explanation: Taking deep breaths to calm down before responding to an angry email (D) is correct because self-regulation is managing your emotions and impulses and responding thoughtfully rather than reacting. Blaming others (A) shows lack of accountability, ignoring feelings completely (B) is suppression, and expressing every emotion immediately (C) shows poor impulse control.

questions.text: If you receive a monthly net income of KES 100,000, how much should be allocated to the "Wants" category?
questions.explanation: Ksh 30,000 (B) is correct because in the 50-30-20 budgeting rule 50% goes to needs, 30% to wants and 20% to savings and debt. 30% of KES 100,000 is KES 30,000. KES 50,000 (A) is the needs share and KES 20,000 (C) is the savings share. KES 10,000 (D) is 10%, which is not part of the rule.

questions.text: A HCA is feeling overwhelmed by an increased workload. What is the most appropriate step?

options.A: Communicate the concerns to the manager and discuss task prioritization
options.B: Isolate self and work alone at a faster rate so that assigned task is finished
options.C: Disregard some patient requests to lighten the load
options.D: Complain to other staff members during the shift

questions.explanation: Communicate the concerns to the manager and discuss task prioritization (A) is correct because speaking to the supervisor is a professional and constructive way to get help, reorganise tasks and keep patients safe. Working alone faster (B) risks mistakes, ignoring patient requests (C) is neglect, and complaining to colleagues (D) does not solve the problem and harms team morale.

questions.text: An apathetic audience or patient is one who:

options.A: Is angry and actively rejects your message
options.B: Does not have enough facts to form an opinion
options.C: Already knows everything about the topic
options.D: Knows about the topic but feels it is not relevant

questions.explanation: Knows about the topic but feels it is not relevant (D) is correct because an apathetic audience is indifferent or uninterested; they may know the subject but do not see why it matters to them, so the speaker must show relevance and make the message interesting. An angry audience that rejects the message (A) is hostile, one without enough facts (B) is uninformed, and one that already knows everything (C) is a knowledgeable audience.

questions.text: A registered nurse has delegated tasks to a HCA. Which task should be completed first?

options.C: Assisting a stable patient with ambulation
options.D: Taking vital signs of a patient with breathing difficulties

questions.explanation: Taking vital signs of a patient with breathing difficulties (D) is correct because airway and breathing problems are life-threatening and take priority, and the HCA should report abnormal findings to the nurse immediately. Making an unoccupied bed (A), restocking supplies (B) and assisting a stable patient to walk (C) are non-urgent tasks that can wait.

questions.text: An example of interpersonal quality of a leader is:
questions.explanation: Delegation (C) is the best answer because interpersonal qualities are the skills used in working with other people, such as communication, delegation, empathy, team building and motivating others. Courage (A), resilience (B) and integrity (D) are personal (intrapersonal) qualities that describe the leader's character. If your lecture notes classify these differently, follow your notes.

questions.text: In decision-making steps, the last step is:
questions.explanation: Review results (C) is correct because the decision-making process is: identify the problem, gather information, identify alternatives, weigh the alternatives and choose, implement the decision, and finally review (evaluate) the results to see if it worked. Gathering information (A) and identifying alternatives (B) come early, and implementation (D) comes before the review.

questions.text: Which is the most reliable indicator of pain in palliative care?
questions.explanation: The patient's own report (A) is correct because pain is subjective: it is what the patient says it is, so their own description and rating (for example on a 0 to 10 scale) is the most reliable indicator. Observation (B) and facial expression (D) are used when the patient cannot speak, and blood pressure (C) can change for many reasons and is not a reliable indicator of pain.
